content: 1. Cervical Priming Prior to Induced Surgical Abortion: A Cochrane review, conducted by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2021 (unpublished), evaluated the use of osmotic dilators or medications for cervical priming before surgical abortion. This review focused on the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in preparing the cervix for the procedure. 2. Vacuum Aspiration for Abortions at Less Than 14 Weeks: An updated Cochrane review by Kim C, Barnard S, Park MH, and Ngo TD in 2021 (forthcoming) examined the use of vacuum aspiration for all indications of abortion under 14 weeks of gestation. This included its application in managing incomplete abortions, with a focus on safety and efficacy. 3. Dilation and Evacuation (D&E) for Surgical Abortions at 14 Weeks or More: A new systematic review by Feyssa M and Kim C in 2021 (unpublished) assessed the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of second-trimester abortions performed by mid-level providers using the dilation and evacuation method. 4. Medical Abortion at Less Than 12 Weeks: An updated Cochrane review by Kim C, Barnard S, Park MH, and Ngo TD in 2021 (forthcoming) explored the eligibility criteria, medication administration, and outcome assessment for medical abortions performed before 12 weeks of gestation. 5. Medical Abortion at 12 Weeks or More: A new systematic review by Feyssa M and Kim C in 2021 (unpublished) evaluated the effectiveness, safety, and acceptability of second-trimester medical abortions facilitated by mid-level providers. 6. Medical Management of Intrauterine Fetal Demise (IUFD): A Cochrane review by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2020 (unpublished) examined the roles of health workers in providing safe abortion care and post-abortion contraception, specifically focusing on the medical management of IUFD. 7. Medical Management of Incomplete Abortion: An updated Cochrane review by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2020 (unpublished) analyzed the roles of health workers in managing incomplete abortions and providing post-abortion contraception. 8. Delivery of Injectable Contraceptives: An updated Cochrane review by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2020 (unpublished) focused on the roles of health workers in delivering injectable contraceptives as part of safe abortion care and post-abortion contraception. 9. Telemedicine for Medical Abortion Care: An updated Cochrane review by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2020 (unpublished) investigated the use of telemedicine in providing comprehensive medical abortion care or its individual components. 10. Community-Based Outreach Models for Abortion Care: A new systematic review by Villanueva G, Probyn K, Bergman H, Petkovic J, Cogo E, Buckley B, and others in 2021 (unpublished) evaluated community outreach models for providing safe abortion care and post-abortion contraception. 11. Harm-Reduction Counseling for Unsafe Abortions: A new systematic review by Stifani B, Gill R, and Kim C in 2021 (manuscript under review) examined harm-reduction counseling strategies aimed at reducing the risks associated with unsafe abortions. 12. Social Marketing Outreach for Safe Abortion Services: A new systematic review by Abubeker F, Tufa T, and Kim C in 2021 (unpublished) assessed the impact of social marketing interventions on the accessibility and utilization of safe abortion services. 13. Self-Sourcing of Medications for Induced Abortion: A new systematic review by Abubeker F, Tufa T, and Kim C in 2021 (unpublished) evaluated the safety, effectiveness, and acceptability of self-sourcing medications for induced abortion through online services. 14. Self-Administration of Injectable Contraceptives Post-Abortion: An updated Cochrane review by Villanueva G, Bergman H, Cogo E, Petkovic J, Buckley B, Probyn K, and others in 2020 (unpublished) explored the roles of health workers in supporting the self-administration of injectable contraceptives during the post-abortion period. 15. Prophylactic Antibiotics for First-Trimester Abortions: An existing review by Low N, Mueller M, Van Vliet HAAM, and Kapp N in 2012 (updated evidence review conducted in 2021) analyzed the use of perioperative antibiotics to prevent infections following first-trimester abortions. 16. Pre-Abortion Ultrasound: An existing review by Kulier R and Kapp N in 2011 (updated evidence review conducted in April 2021) provided a comprehensive analysis of the use of pre-procedure ultrasound for firstand second-trimester abortions. 17. Surgical Methods for First-Trimester Abortions: An existing review by Kulier R, Cheng L, Fekih A, Hofmeyr GJ, and Campana A in 2001 (updated evidence review conducted in April 2021) examined surgical methods for terminating pregnancies during the first trimester. 18. Medical Management of Induced Abortion: An existing review by Abubeker FA, Lavelanet A, Rodriguez MI, and Kim C in 2020 evaluated medical termination of pregnancy in the early first trimester (≤63 days) using mifepristone and misoprostol or misoprostol alone. An updated review by Whitehouse K, Brant A, Sporstol Fonhus M, Lavelanet A, Ganatra B, and others in 2020 focused on medical regimens for abortion at 12 weeks and beyond. 19. Post-Abortion Follow-Up: Existing reviews by Grossman D, Ellertson C, Grimes DA, and Walker D in 2004, and Grossman D and Grindlay K in 2011 (updated evidence review conducted in April 2021), explored routine follow-up visits after first-trimester induced abortions and alternatives to ultrasound for follow-up after medication abortion. 20. Gestational Age Limits for Abortion: A PICO question addressed the impact of gestational age limits on delayed abortion, continuation of pregnancy, opportunity costs, unlawful abortion, self-managed abortion, and other related outcomes for pregnant individuals and medical professionals. 21. Criminalization of Abortion: A PICO question investigated the effects of criminalizing abortion on delayed abortion, continuation of pregnancy, opportunity costs, unlawful abortion, self-managed abortion, and other outcomes for pregnant individuals and healthcare providers. 22. Grounds-Based Approaches to Abortion Access: A PICO question examined the impact of limiting abortion access based on specific grounds, including delayed abortion, continuation of pregnancy, opportunity costs, unlawful abortion, and other related outcomes. These descriptions provide a detailed and professional summary of the reviews and studies mentioned in the original text.
